title: because
gist: I ran preregistered experiments on what makes Claude Code follow its instructions. Reasons came back inconclusive, no wording factor survives correction on average, and for skills the listing budget in the Claude Code docs controls whether a description reaches the model.
summary: Tells you which edits to a CLAUDE.md or a skill description change what Claude Code does, with the data, the checkers and the harness to rerun them.

hero_image.alt: Line chart of skill load rate at 300 skills with late names. At the CLI's own budget, the minimal description loads at 53% [38, 68] and the long trigger list at 29% [12, 46]. With the budget raised to 100,000 characters, minimal loads at 82% [67, 98] and the trigger list at 99% [97, 100].

site.eyebrow: Preregistered experiments · four studies · Claude Code 2.1.303 · MIT
site.blurb: Anyone who writes a CLAUDE.md or a skill gets plenty of advice about wording, and I ran four preregistered experiments on Claude Code to see which of it changes anything. A reason written for the rule reads as inconclusive at +0.2 points [-5.2, +5.7], and no wording factor survives correction on average, though single rules do move in a post hoc look. For skills, a long description on a never-used skill that sorts after the listing budget is spent doesn't reach the model, and raising the budget the docs describe moved that skill by +69.8 points [+53.7, +85.8], at $0.134 per run against $0.060.
